Overlaying the FOMC’s May 2, 2018 statement with contemporaneous SLOOS readings reinforces a cautiously positive, gradualist stance. The SLOOS points to modest easing in C&I lending standards for large and middle‑market firms and steady-to-improving business loan demand, which supports the statement’s view of solid labor markets and ongoing business fixed investment. At the same time, banks reported tighter standards for certain consumer categories (notably credit cards and auto) and some tightening/softer demand in CRE, suggesting pockets of restraint on household- and property‑related credit.

Taken together with the Financial Stability Report’s note on elevated asset valuations and rising nonfinancial business leverage—but offset by strong bank capital and liquidity—the SLOOS tilts the outlook slightly more constructive for growth via business credit channels, while still validating the “balanced risks” and gradual normalization framing.

Net: modestly positive and a touch firmer than the FSR-only read, but still constrained by sectoral tightening and stability considerations.
